before: Enacted 2024 as Chapter 238 of the Acts of 2024; codified data-center sales/use tax exemption at G.L. c. 64H Section 6(zz) remains in force as of 2026-07-31
after: Approved in part as Chapter 238 on 2024-11-20; section 214 is listed as effective 2024-11-20, and the published exemption applies to costs incurred after that date (observed 2026-11-07).

before: Creates sales/use tax exemption for qualified data center equipment, software, electricity, and construction costs; 20-year qualification period; 100,000-square-foot and $50 million thresholds.
after: Sales and use tax exemption for eligible equipment, software, electricity and construction costs for qualified data centers; at least 100,000 aggregate square feet, $50 million in qualified costs within 10 years of certification, and at least 100 Massachusetts jobs; facility and building qualification periods are 20 years under specified anchors.
Facility/building-specific 20-year qualification periods, subject to certification and statutory anchors; not a sunset of paragraph (zz).

before: Accompanied a study order (H.5324) 2026-04-06; effectively shelved for the remainder of the 194th General Court
after: Accompanied a study order, H.5324, on 2026-04-06; last action displayed in the official H.4144 history as observed 2026-11-07.

before: Broad energy affordability and grid bill; not a data center moratorium bill, but addresses load growth, grid planning, and utility infrastructure cost allocation.
after: Proposes energy affordability and grid measures, including flexible interconnection and stakeholder recommendations on infrastructure financing and customer connections, with data center representatives included.

before: Reported favorably by Joint Committee on Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity 2025-12-24; discharged from Joint Rules and referred to House Rules Committee 2026-01-08; pending as of 2026-07-31
after: Reported favorably 2025-12-24 and discharged to House Rules 2026-01-08; last action displayed in official history as observed 2026-11-07.

before: Creates a special legislative commission to study load growth due to AI and data centers, including high-performance computing and electrification demand.
after: Would establish a legislative commission to study electricity demand from data centers supporting high-performance computing and AI, industrial growth, and transportation and building electrification; report due one year after passage.

before: Referred to House Rules Committee 2025-12-11; no further action recorded as of 2026-07-31
after: Referred to House Rules 2025-12-11; the official docket displayed one action when observed 2026-11-07.

before: Would add G.L. c. 164 Section 152 to prevent residential and income-eligible customers from bearing increased electric costs caused by large or qualified data centers; covered facilities include sites able to use 10 MW or more.
after: Would add G.L. c. 164 section 152: distribution companies could not reduce electricity availability or increase rates for residential or income-eligible customers due to covered data centers, defined in part as able to use at least 10 MW; requires departmental rate review and company records.

before: Reported favorably from Joint Committee on Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity as new-draft S.2630, referred to Senate Ways and Means 2025-10-16; pending as of 2026-07-31
after: S.37 accompanied new draft S.2630 on 2025-10-16; S.2630 was reported favorably and referred to Senate Ways and Means that date, the last actions displayed when observed 2026-11-07.

before: AI economic development and safety bill with compute-related provisions; not a data center moratorium bill.
after: S.37 proposed AI safety, covered-model and computing-cluster duties and an innovation fund; its new draft S.2630 proposed frontier-model transparency and safety duties, the fund, and a public-compute framework. Neither proposes a data-center moratorium.
